Yes, Hawaiians had their own measurement system. They used units of measurement called "anakahi" which were based on different parts of the body. According to the lesson plans provided, these units included anana, muku, iwilei, haʻilima, pīʻā, and kīkoʻo. According to the lesson plan, Hawaiians used hōkū (star navigation) to find their way across the ocean. They built strong sails from woven lauhala mats and learned how to steer their canoes using the wind. Just like Maui, they worked with the wind, using it to travel across the vast Pacific Ocean and find new islands. /  / Source: L3 Kiʻi Pōhaku (Grade 4–5).
